correctness.rationale: Using the known symmetric-gate exact mean time T_h(x), independently checked the two expressions and root equations. B(x)=(exp x-1)/x² is uniformly coercive; rare-limit E_h=T_h-1/(2h) is bounded below by B. The compact C² expansions H+hJ and B+exp(x)/(x sqrt(2h)) imply convergence of all global minimizers to unique nondegenerate roots x_s=1.6244614336663, x_b=1.5936242600400; local implicit-function uniqueness follows at sufficiently small/large h. IFT expansions x_s-0.2262351716h+O(h²), and x_b-x_b/sqrt(2h)+O(h^-1) have opposite sides of x_b, forcing nonmonotonicity without all-h uniqueness. Independent numerical minimization at h=.0005,.001,.01,100,10000 agreed with limiting directions and scales. Finite samples do not prove global branch behavior.
